content:
This publish-safe library follows a fictional group building a living guide to
their neighborhood. It is deliberately connected: people know one another,
projects create tasks and events, journal entries point back to decisions, and
the same ideas appear in the Canvas workspace.

> Start with the [Castle feature tour](/note/wiki/castle_feature_tour), then open the
> relationship graph and follow any person or note link that catches your eye.

## Six good places to begin

| Explore | What it demonstrates |
| --- | --- |
| [Graph field guide](/note/wiki/graph_field_guide) | Relationship colors, groups, departments, and direct links |
| [Neighborhood Atlas](/note/projects/neighborhood_atlas/neighborhood_atlas) | A project connected to people, tasks, events, and research |
| [Why third places matter](/note/notes/research/third_places) | A link-rich research note with citations and backlinks |
| [Field day journal](/note/journal/2026-08-27_field_day) | A dated narrative with an original field illustration |
| [Consent and care](/note/notes/consent_and_care) | A practical policy note with tasks, events, and follow-up links |
| [The stash](/note/stash/wayfinding_reference) | Quick captures for articles, videos, ideas, and loose follow-ups |

## The story so far

[Alex Morgan](/note/people/alex_morgan) and [Jamie Chen](/note/people/jamie_chen) began by
mapping the places that make a neighborhood feel welcoming. [Maya Singh](/note/people/maya_singh)
turned the research into a visual language, while [Noah Williams](/note/people/noah_williams)
built a lightweight data pipeline. Community hosts [Sofia Rossi](/note/people/sofia_rossi)
and [Amara Okafor](/note/people/amara_okafor) keep the work grounded in real conversations.

Their current focus is the [Neighborhood Atlas](/note/projects/neighborhood_atlas/neighborhood_atlas).
The earlier [Listening Garden](/note/projects/listening_garden/listening_garden) is complete,
and the [Mobile Story Booth](/note/projects/mobile_story_booth/mobile_story_booth) is waiting
for its next planning window.

After the open studio, the group is preparing a
[community listening session](/note/events/2026/community_listening_session) to decide
which observations should shape the next public draft.

## Markdown sampler

- [x] Follow an internal `[[wiki link]]`
- [ ] Search for “serendipity”
- [ ] Open the backlinks panel on this note
- [ ] Switch the Library between list and graph views
- [ ] Open the example Canvas

### A small code block

```ts
const castle = {
  sourceOfTruth: "Markdown",
  connections: "Obsidian-style links",
  storage: "local-first",
};
```

Everything here is synthetic. The names, organizations, events, and plans exist
only to make Castle pleasant to explore.
